title: User profile API with serde models
name: User profile endpoints

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how request bodies are deserialized and applied to user records? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A caller POSTs to /users with a body that also contains `"roles": ["admin"]`. What does the extractor do?
choices: The extra field is ignored and the user is created with no roles.
The extra field is applied because UserRecord has a roles field.
Deserialization fails because of deny_unknown_fields and axum responds with a 4xx before the handler body runs.
The handler returns 403 because roles are not allowed.

questions.prompt: A client sends PATCH /users/me with `{"display_name": null}`. What is the effect on the stored record?
choices: display_name is cleared to an empty string.
The request is rejected because null is not a valid String.
The display name becomes the string "null".
display_name is unchanged, because null and an absent field both deserialize to None.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the JSON returned in the responses is correct?
choices: password_hash is omitted because of skip_serializing, and roles appear as lowercase strings such as "member".
password_hash is included but redacted, and roles appear as numeric enum indexes.
password_hash is omitted only on create; update responses include it.
created_at is serialized as a Unix timestamp integer.
